name: Your Company
tagline: Specialty coffee roasted in Tashkent every Tuesday

seo.title: Your Company — specialty coffee and roastery in Tashkent
seo.description: We roast specialty beans every Tuesday and deliver across Tashkent within a day. Café in Mirabad, bean subscriptions, barista courses.
seo.answer: Your Company is a roastery and café in Tashkent at 22 Mirabad St. We roast specialty beans every Tuesday: a 250 g bag costs from 145,000 UZS, delivery across Tashkent is next day and free over 300,000 UZS. The café is open daily from 8:00.

listing.description: A website for a café, coffee roaster or bakery. Bags of beans on a shelf with tasting notes and prices, steam over a cup in WebGL, a café menu, a bean subscription and the journey from farm to cup.

sections.title: Coffee that smells of the farm, not the warehouse
sections.subtitle: We bring green beans straight from small farms, roast them in small batches on Tuesdays and sell them while the coffee still has character.

sections.label: About us
sections.title: A small roastery with a big stubborn streak
sections.text: We started in 2021 with a five-kilo roaster in a garage in Chilanzar. Today we roast up to 300 kilos a week, but the rules haven’t changed: we know every farm by name, cup every batch and never sell coffee more than a month after roasting. At the Mirabad café you can try any bean from the shelf — as filter, espresso or AeroPress.

items.q: How fast do you deliver beans?
items.a: Within Tashkent, the day after you order — free over 300,000 UZS, otherwise 25,000 UZS. To other cities in Uzbekistan, 2–4 days by courier service.
Yes, for free. Tell us your brewing method — cezve, espresso, filter, French press or moka pot — and we’ll grind to suit it.

items.q: How long do the beans keep?
items.a: Coffee opens up best between day 5 and day 30 after roasting. Keep the bag closed at room temperature, not in the fridge.

items.q: Which bean should I choose for a cezve or moka pot?
items.a: Go for Brazil Cerrado or the espresso blend: chocolate and nutty notes handle high temperatures well.
Yes, once a month: a 3-day basic course of 3 hours a day, 1,900,000 UZS, groups of up to 6. We post the schedule on Telegram.

items.q: Do you work with cafés and restaurants?
items.a: Yes, we supply beans from 3 kg a week, set up equipment and train baristas. Write to us and we’ll send samples for cupping.
